Canada.fact: Payments Canada successfully launched Lynx Release 2 in March 2023, migrating Canada's high-value payment system to the ISO 20022 messaging standard to support rich data transmission and automated transaction compliance.

Payments Canada officially launched the Real-Time Rail (RTR) on November 9, 2026—operating 24/7/365 on ISO 20022 messaging with centralized Confirmation of Payee fraud controls—following its November 8, 2026 designation by the Bank of Canada as a prominent payment system under the Payment Clearing and Settlement Act.
Canada.source: Payments Canada & Bank of Canada RTR Launch Designation (Nov 2026)

Canada.fact: Under Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) supervisory framework administered by the Bank of Canada and amendments to the Canadian Payments Act, registered non-bank Payment Service Providers (PSPs) gained regulatory pathways for direct participation in Payments Canada clearing systems including the Real-Time Rail.
Canada.source: Bank of Canada Retail Payment Supervision Framework

Australia.fact: Australia's New Payments Platform (NPP) successfully completed its industry-wide migration of high-value payments messaging to the ISO 20022 standard in March 2023 and scaled its PayTo digital account-to-account mandate service for real-time corporate and retail settlement.
Australia.source: Reserve Bank of Australia Payments System Board Report

Australia.fact: The Reserve Bank of Australia and Australian Payments Plus (AP+) utilize the ISO 20022 standard across the NPP to support structured remittance details and international inbound payment verification, reducing compliance friction for cross-border transactions.
Australia.source: RBA Bulletin: Modernising Australia's High-Value Payments System

China.fact: China's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) clears and settles cross-border Renminbi (RMB) transactions on ISO 20022 messaging standards, expanding to over 1,800 direct and indirect banking participants across more than 133 countries and territories by Q3 2026.

The People's Bank of China (PBOC) expanded its digital yuan (e-CNY) operating network to 30 commercial banks in 2026 and upgraded e-CNY into a programmable digital deposit money framework with smart contract trade settlement, alongside the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) Project Ensemble 24/7 tokenized Central Bank Money (CeBM) interbank pilot.
China.source: PBOC e-CNY & HKMA Project Ensemble Progress Reports (2026)

Switzerland.fact: Switzerland's Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) system, operated by SIX under the supervision of the Swiss National Bank (SNB), operates on the ISO 20022-based SIC5 platform, enforcing mandatory instant payment capability across Swiss financial institutions.

Swiss commodity traders (e.g., Glencore, Trafigura) settle physical shipments utilizing structured trade finance instruments, including digital Letters of Credit (LCs) clearing through European transaction banking networks.

Under Project Helvetia Phase III, the Swiss National Bank (SNB) and SIX Digital Exchange (SDX) extended live issuance and settlement of wholesale central bank digital currency (wCBDC) in Swiss francs on regulated distributed ledger infrastructure through 2026.
Switzerland.source: Swiss National Bank Project Helvetia III Release

UK.fact: The Bank of England migrated its Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system and CHAPS clearing network to the ISO 20022 messaging standard and transitioned to the renewed RTGS core ledger engine (TS3) to enhance resiliency, direct API access, and tokenized collateral clearing.
UK.source: Bank of England RTGS Renewal Program

UK.fact: The London Metal Exchange (LME) clears physical metal trades through LME Clear, utilizing multi-currency liquidity accounts and bank guarantees to mitigate clearing broker counterparty credit risk.

Global.fact: Project mBridge, a multi-currency cross-border wholesale CBDC platform developed by the BIS Innovation Hub and founding central banks, reached its Minimum Viable Product (MVP) stage in June 2024 and transitioned toward commercial multi-corridor trade settlement.

SWIFT concluded the multi-year coexistence period between legacy MT messages and ISO 20022 for cross-border payments and reporting (CBPR+) in November 2025, establishing ISO 20022 as the mandatory global wire baseline while running parallel tokenized ledger interoperability trials with global banks in 2026.

Project Agorá, convened by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) and the Institute of International Finance (IIF), unites seven major central banks and over 40 private financial institutions in 2025-2026 to test atomic cross-border wholesale settlement combining tokenized commercial bank deposits with tokenized central bank reserves.
Global.source: BIS Innovation Hub Project Agorá Blueprint

Global.fact: Project Nexus (incorporated in Singapore as Nexus Global Payments by founding ASEAN and Reserve Bank of India central banks) links domestic Instant Payment Systems (IPS) through a multilateral hub-and-spoke ISO 20022 gateway for real-time cross-border retail and commercial settlement.
Global.source: BIS Project Nexus & Nexus Global Payments

Global.fact: The U.S. Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act and European MiCA regulations establish federal and supranational prudential standards—including 1:1 liquid reserve backing and redemption mandates—for regulated payment stablecoins used in institutional cross-border settlement.
Global.source: OCC & Federal Reserve GENIUS Act Implementation Framework (2026)
